ns_bug_city.blurb: Bug City is a small day crag near Peggys Cove Village on Nova Scotia's Atlantic coast. Its eleven routes mix mostly bolted lines with a few gear-protected ones, and a handful can also be set up on a top rope. The grades run from easy fifth class at 5.7 up to a couple of 5.11s, with a decent cluster in the 5.8 to 5.9 range, so there is something for newer leaders as well as people looking for a hard pull. The gear routes are a good place for beginners to learn. Locals single it out as a good choice in fall and winter.

ri_peace_dove_boulder.blurb: Peace Dove Boulder sits in the Lincoln Woods bouldering zone a few miles north of Providence, in a small cluster that holds just two boulders. It has eleven problems, from an easy V0 up to a V8, with the middle of the range around V3 to V5 and a few harder lines above that. The Peace Dove line itself is the one most climbers come for, and its neighbour Warhawk is the other headline problem. Lincoln Woods is known for high quality bouldering on sharply textured stone, so expect friction-heavy skin wear.

ri_streambed_boulder_the.blurb: The Streambed Boulder is a gentle warm-up stop in the Talus Area at Lincoln Woods, close to Providence. It holds eleven problems, all easy: most are V0 and V1 with a few reaching V2 or V3. The climbing is mainly slabs and faces on positive holds, though a handful of lines are trickier than they look. It sits just above a small stream and below the Redeemer boulder, and it is the quickest boulder in this zone to reach, which makes it a handy first stop for beginners or a place to loosen up before harder projects nearby.
